sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
Operating income compounded at 4.1% [F202] and net income at 0.5% [F203]; the cited passages do not explain that gap.
Operating margin fell 11.9pp to 8.1% in FY2019 [D109][F23] after an $8.35 billion impairment [X112] that the 10-K ties to currency devaluations, slower category growth and competition [P62].
Operating margin rebounded 14.0pp to 22.1% in FY2020 [D160][F24], mostly because of the prior-year impairment base effect, which the 10-K puts at $8.3 billion [P71].
Non-US geography supplied 3.1pp of FY2026's 3.3% growth [D511][D457]; the US added 0.1pp [D536].
The 10-K attributes FY2026 net sales growth to favourable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26][F10].
Beauty was the largest segment contributor at 1.3pp [D603], growing 7.1% [D602] on an 18.4% share of revenue [D601].
Operating income fell 3.4% [D458] on 3.3% revenue growth [D457], an incremental margin of -25.6% [D481].
Diluted EPS rose 1.7% [D461] against 0.5% net income growth [D459], as diluted shares fell 1.3% [D476].
Operating margin of 22.7% [F30] sits above its 22.1% median [D648], below the 24.3% FY2025 high [D647] and well above the 8.1% low [D646].
The 1.6pp fall [D470] reflects cost of revenue -1.0pp [D483], SG&A -0.6pp [D485], R&D +0.1pp [D484] and other lines -0.1pp [D486].
The 10-K attributes the decline primarily to lower gross margin and higher marketing spending [P25], with cost of revenue at 49.8% of revenue [D435] against 48.8% [D384].
In FY2020, other lines explain 12.1pp of the 14.0pp rise [D176][D160].
Other income rose to $1.08 billion from $154 million [X108][X107] on the Glad joint venture gain [P24], so net margin of 18.4% [F50] fell only 0.5pp [D471].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion [F80] was 1.22x net income [D444], and free cash flow of $15.1 billion [F100] was 0.94x [D445], below the 1.02x window median [D660].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% [D441] is just above its 17.2% median [D654], while capex of $4.41 billion [F90] was 1.40x D&A [D446].
The 10-K says working capital added only $29 million [P3], with inventory consuming $641 million for safety stock and payables adding $919 million [P3].
Operating cash flow fell 10.2% in FY2025 to $17.8 billion [D411][F79]; the cited filings do not explain that fall.
Net cash of -$24.2 billion [D450], or -27.8% of revenue [D451], ranks at the 33rd percentile of six staples peers [D676], against a peer median of -1.0% [D677].
Long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion [D468][F190], while the current portion rose to $6.46 billion [X194].
Buybacks of $5.03 billion [X134] and dividends of $10.2 billion [X144] totalled $15.3 billion [D452], or 100.7% of free cash flow [D453], while diluted shares fell 1.3% [D476].
With net debt already heavier relative to revenue than the peer median [D451][D677], a weaker cash year would push distributions onto debt.
Buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in nine of ten years (R2), from 132.8% in FY2017 [D19] to 100.7% in FY2026 [D453], with FY2024 the only exception at 86.6% [D350].
The 10-K says unit volume and mix were unchanged in FY2026 [P26], so growth of 3.3% [D457] rested on price and currency while cost of revenue grew 5.3% [D472].
Price-led growth that does not cover cost increases [D483] risks further compressing operating margin.
The current ratio candidate (R1) is benign on its own: the ratio has stayed between 0.63x and 0.88x [D661][D662], and FY2026's 0.68x [F180] is close to the 0.72x median [D663].
An FY2027 10-K showing operating margin below the 22.1% window median [D648] would confirm the margin is trending down from the FY2026 level of 22.7% [F30].
A payout below 100.7% of free cash flow [D453] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm easing; a reading above it would confirm the pressure.
Cost of revenue at or below 48.8% of revenue [D384] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the gross-margin fall has reversed; a level above 49.8% [D435] would confirm it has persisted.
